headline_marked: Deep [[depression forms in Bay]], ports on alert
headline: Deep depression forms in Bay, ports on alert
summary: A low-pressure system has intensified into a deep depression, prompting warning signal No. 3 for several sea ports.
details: A low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into a deep depression. The system is currently moving northwest across the west-central and adjoining northwest Bay.
// a deep depression is a weather system that typically brings heavy rain and gusty winds, and as a result, sea ports are on alert. //
At 9pm Tuesday, the deep depression was located 875km southwest of Chattogram, 850km southwest of Cox’s Bazar, 695km southwest of Mongla, and 720km southwest of Payra.
Winds within 48km of the center are reaching 50kmph, rising to 60kmph in gusts. This may result in rough seas near the center of the system.

Chattogram, Cox’s Bazar, Mongla, and Payra ports have been asked to keep local warning signal No. 3 hoisted. Fishing boats and trawlers in the north Bay have been advised to remain close to the coast.

Meteorologist Khandaker Hafizur Rahman told bdnews24.com that while it is not likely to develop into a cyclone for now, its influence may bring rain to the southern and southwestern parts of the country.
The system is expected to move further west and northwest, crossing India’s north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coast by Wednesday midnight.

headline_marked: Fuel price hike: [[Launch and truck fares raised]] before govt nod
headline: Fuel price hike: Launch and truck fares raised before govt nod
summary: Transport operators are increasing charges following a Tk 20 per litre rise in fuel prices, despite warnings from the government.
details: Following a Tk 20 per litre hike in retail prices of diesel, octane, petrol, and kerosene, launch and truck operators have already started increasing fares before official government approval.
caption:
Fuel prices jump by Tk 20 per litre, and transport fares are already climbing—even before the government has officially approved the new rates.

Following a Tk 20 per litre hike in retail prices of diesel, octane, petrol, and kerosene, launch and truck operators have already started increasing fares before official government approval.
